correctness.rationale: The complete dominating-set condition is that selected cells meet all rows or all columns. Under 2|D|<=pq, an equal-size rival exists if the complement meets all rows, or, after a complete selected row is forced, if it meets all columns. This establishes both directions of the full-row-and-column classification; above half no rival fits. Two independently derived inclusion-exclusion expressions count full-line events and domination events. The sharp minimum follows from 2(p+q-2)<=pq; p=2 and (3,3) are exhaustively handled above half. The standalone verifier tested the original definition on 10064 masks and structural/counting formulae on an additional 1409024 masks, plus 95 parameter checks; finite tests are expressly not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact two-parameter classification resolves all accurate-dominating-set cardinalities for the natural line graph of K_{p,q}, including a nonlocal disjoint-rival constraint. The half-order threshold links an established general principle to a new geometric low-half obstruction, while the minimum solution space has precise width-two and 3x3 exceptions and generic pq rigidity. This complete natural family classification is useful even without a new downstream theorem, and its low-half part is not a mere restatement of standard domination.
